originality.rationale: Tittmann–Averbouch–Makowsky completely encode the distribution by Q and their Proposition 2 distinguishes individual small trees; this is explicitly acknowledged. However, their inspected results do not prove the new quantified mean/variance universality, sharp path/star extremality and first six-vertex degree-twin third-moment separation. Janson treats asymptotic covariance processes under assumptions and Hackl et al. random labelled trees, not the same all-fixed-tree finite problem. Published scientific-index queries identified no statement whose proof entails the entire sharp claim; residual derivative/reliability-literature overlap risk remains.
residual_risks: The general Q polynomial gives full exact distributions and may have downstream corollaries or tables deriving some or all of the moment facts; independent bibliographic verification remains required.
Older reliability, graph-subset enumeration, or landscape-fragmentation literature could contain equivalent tree moment formulas under different names.

value.rationale: Fragment-count uncertainty is a direct ecological habitat fragmentation quantity. The exact order-uniform path/star risk range quantifies how tree branching changes variability at fixed survival fraction, and the sharp six-patch skewness obstruction proves that degree-based variance equivalence does not imply equal tail asymmetry. The two sampling protocols permit direct analysis of independent patch failures and a fixed patch-budget scenario, without asserting downstream conservation outcomes.
